eld.notes: ESL endorsement codes 488 (K-8), 489 (6-12), 490 (PreK-12). Praxis 5362 required (Professional Assessments Policy 5.105). Two pathways: traditional EPP-approved program, or TDOE's no-cost Additional Endorsement Program for already-licensed teachers (asynchronous coursework + Praxis), authorized under Educator Licensure Policy 5.502 (revised Feb 2025). ESL programs minimum 18 hours, 6 hours of college-level world language, aligned to TESOL P-12 Standards (Policy 5.505 §English as a Second Language). Practicum coded null because Policy 5.505 does not enumerate clinical/practicum hours separately for ESL — set by EPPs. 2024 update: TDOE moved EL assessment from WIDA/ACCESS to ELPA21 effective July 1, 2024 (first ELPA21 Summative Feb 5, 2025) and adopted ELPA21 ELD Standards in place of WIDA 2020. EL share rose from 4.6% (2019 baseline) to ~9% (2024 TDOE figure, 93,433 students).

sei.notes: Rule 0520-01-19-.03(8) requires annual ESL training only for teachers who provide Direct or Indirect ESL Services, not all teachers.

history.description: Retrieved current SBE Policy 5.505 'Literacy and Specialty Area Standards for Educator Preparation' (revised 11/21/2025) and Policy 5.502 'Educator Licensure' (revised 02/21/2025). Policy 5.505 explicitly references diverse instructional practices, students' cultural and linguistic experiences, language/linguistic diversity as a source of strength, culturally relevant and responsive instruction, and English Learners by name (e.g., 'all learners (e.g., English Learners, students with disabilities, and at-risk learners)') in general literacy and early-childhood standards applicable beyond the ESL endorsement. ESL programs are aligned to TESOL P-12 Standards and require instruction on the Tennessee EL Framework. All four professionalStandardsMentions booleans (diverse, cultural, linguistic, el) confirmed true against the current standards document.
